sections.h2: Where to file a deed for Gladwin County land
sections.html:
The register's office sits inside the county building, 401 West Cedar Avenue, Gladwin, MI 48624, alongside the commission chambers. Walk in on a weekday between 8:30 and 4:30, or phone 989-426-7551.

Gladwin County register charges
ServiceCharge
Recording a document$30 flat, any number of pages
Each extra instrument assigned or discharged$3, added to the flat fee
Certification$5
Copies$1 a page
Searches50 cents per year, $5 minimum

Questions about the schedule trace back to MCL 600.2567. The flat charge already covers the state's remonumentation and automation shares.

sections.h2: What to bring when you file
sections.html:
A deed package that arrives complete is recorded without a second trip. Bring the signed original deed, a check for the $30 flat fee, and any extra $3 charges for additional instruments a discharge or assignment covers. If you want a certified copy afterward, add the $5 certification and $1 for each page copied.

Put the value of the sale in the text of the deed, or attach an affidavit that states it. Counter staff can quote the fee schedule. Drafting the deed itself falls to a title company or attorney.

Mailing it in? Phone ahead for the current total, because the amount turns on how many instruments the paper covers. Counter filings are paid on the spot, while e-filings get a one business day grace period.

The register's page links an online land records search and a free fraud alert sign-up, and the office takes electronic recording through three vendors. Paper filings still come in by hand or mail. Call the office to learn which vendors it uses before you submit anything online.

The alert is worth setting up if you own land you rarely visit. Whoever is away from the parcel tends to be the last person to learn that a paper was recorded against it, and the sign-up costs nothing.

Beyond the recording fee, the main charge is transfer tax. A seller pays $4.30 for each $500 of price, made up of $3.75 for the state and 55 cents for the county (the rate for counties with fewer than two million people). The county treasurer must receive it within 15 days after delivery.

The deed carries its value in the text, or an affidavit does. Several transfers sit outside the state levy, among them gifts to a child or grandchild, foreclosure deeds and mortgages. Payment timing follows the filing method, as described above.

Gladwin County is rural and thinly settled, in the middle of the Lower Peninsula, and had an estimated 26,077 residents in 2025. Local government is two cities, Gladwin and Beaverton, and 15 townships. Each has its own treasurer for current bills, so first confirm which township or city your parcel is in.

  • Housing: 17,329 housing units, 11,280 households and an owner-occupancy rate of 86.1%.
  • Rent and value: median gross rent is $690, and the midpoint home value is $162,300.
  • Income: $55,349 for the median household.
  • Permits: 93 building permits in 2025.

Gladwin's land was surveyed under the Northwest Ordinance in the 1830s, and settlement came much later. County government was organized in 1875. Some of the early survey work was faulty, so a seller holding an old legal description should ask the title company to check it against the parcel before closing.

The equalization department's GIS viewer helps locate a parcel on a map. If your description is old, print the viewer's map and the recorded deed together and bring both to your title company, so any mismatch is found while there is still time to record a correction.

sections.h2: How the tax calendar touches a sale
sections.html:
Township and city treasurers bill and collect first. Bills for summer are mailed July 1 and carry no interest through September 14 (Gladwin City runs a different summer schedule). The winter round is mailed December 1 and is due February 14.

Any balance left on March 1 moves to the county, which adds a 4% charge plus one percent interest a month. The county's timeline then shows a $15 mailing fee in October, forfeiture on the next March 1, a personal visit fee, a publication fee in the fall and a last payment date of March 31. Foreclosed parcels go to auction at tax-sale.info. Postmarks don't count. Payment is dated the day the county receives and processes it.

The treasurer also certifies deeds, plat maps and tax histories, so order a payoff and history before a sale. For principal residence, taxable value, hardship and veteran questions, ask the township or city assessor.

Equalization is a county department that reviews local assessments on behalf of the Board of Commissioners. Using an annual study, it aims to hold each property class in each local unit at 49% to 50% of true cash value. The local assessor stays responsible for fairness between individual parcels.

  • April: equalization report of values.
  • June: millage reduction fractions for each taxing authority.
  • October: apportionment report of allowable millage rates.
  • December 31: the sales and appraisal study.

The department also maintains the countywide database of values, descriptions, title changes, owner addresses and exemption status, plus a GIS viewer for locating land records and principal residence exemption forms. A deed recorded at the register shows up there as a title change, so a buyer should send in a change of address form after closing.

sections.h2: Selling when tax is still owed
sections.html:
A sale can proceed. The closing agent settles the overdue amount out of the seller's proceeds, based on a payoff that runs to the day of closing.

Timing matters because costs step up. Once a parcel forfeits, monthly interest goes from 1% to 1.5% retroactive to the original delinquency date, and a personal visit and publication fee follow. Redemption rights end at the close of business on March 31, so a seller near that date should request the payoff first. Buyers paying cash as-is can often close quickly when repairs or an inheritance stall a listing.

If the sale is a cash deal with a buyer who wants to move fast, the same payoff and certification still come first, because the closing agent needs both either way. Sellers who inherited a house and are still sorting out the title should ask the title company to review the recorded chain before listing. Steps that keep a sale moving:

  1. Ask the county treasurer for a payoff and a tax history.
  2. Pass both to the closing agent.
  3. Check that the deed carries its value or an affidavit.
  4. Pay the transfer tax to the county treasurer within 15 days of delivery.

faqs.q: What is the flat recording charge at the Gladwin County Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: It is $30 per document, whether the document runs one page or many. A discharge or assignment that covers several instruments adds $3 for each extra one.

faqs.q: When can I visit the Gladwin County Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: The office is open weekdays from 8:30 in the morning until 4:30 in the afternoon at 401 West Cedar Avenue. The telephone number is 989-426-7551.

faqs.q: Does the Gladwin office take e-filings?
faqs.a: Yes. The county works with three e-recording vendors. Call the office to learn which vendors it uses before you submit anything online.

faqs.q: Who owes the transfer tax on a Gladwin County sale?
faqs.a: The seller owes it. The combined state and county rate is $4.30 per $500 of price, paid to the county treasurer within 15 days after the deed is delivered.

faqs.q: When does overdue Gladwin County tax go to the county?
faqs.a: On March 1 of the following year. A 4% fee and monthly interest of one percent start then, and the parcel can forfeit a year later.
